name: Europejara
sum: The first European tapejarid, from the Barremian Las Hoyas Lagerstätte of Cuenca, Spain — at its description the oldest known toothless pterosaur.
wsnote: About 2 m in the 2012 description; revised to 3–4 m in 2023 by some of the same authors.
holotype: MCCM-LH 9413 — La Huérguina Formation, Las Hoyas, Cuenca, Spain.
material: Rear of the skull with almost complete lower jaws, compressed on slab and counterslab.
biology: Tapejarids are thought to have eaten fruit and seeds (perhaps also insects and small vertebrates); Europejara's age led its describers to suggest a role in seed dispersal of early flowering plants.
author: Vullo et al. 2012
